title: Modular support add-ons, hotfix SLA & rolling-upgrade cadence for Private/VPC licensing
creator: Maya Chen
description: Run an experiment for a modular license and support product for Private/VPC and on-prem customers. Proposal: base license (install+core runtime) + optional support add-ons (Standard, Priority, Hotfix SLA, Upgrade Window, Security Questionnaire Response Pack). Define pricing bands, contract language for entitlements, and a cadence for rolling upgrades and hotfixes. Outcome should reduce sales friction for regulated customers while preserving predictable revenue and limiting operational exposure.
background: Sales and Solutions Engineering report that large regulated buyers often stall on: (1) frequency and responsibility for security patches / hotfixes, (2) upgrade windows and associated downtime risk, and (3) clarity on what is included in on-prem licensing vs professional services. Current monolithic license + bespoke SOW flow is slow and high-effort for Redwood. Several RFIs include security questionnaire tasks that our CS team spends hours responding to. We need a modular packaging approach to standardize offerings and accelerate procurement.
proposal_summary: Introduce a three-tier modular support offering sold as license add-ons: (A) Standard Support (business hours, next-business-day), (B) Priority Support (24/7 critical response, 4-hour P1 SLA), (C) Hotfix SLA (guaranteed hotfix delivery within defined window, paid annual opt-in). Add two entitlements: Upgrade Window (quarterly scheduled rolling upgrades with optional maintenance window coordination) and Security Questionnaire Response Pack (pre-filled templates + dedicated review hours). Price each addon as a clear per-cluster/year fee and create combinable SKUs.
acceptance_criteria: Published draft SKUs and price bands for base license and 5 support add-ons
Sample contract language (SLA, entitlements, responsibilities) approved by legal
Security Questionnaire Response Pack templated and reviewed by security
Pilot agreement signed with two sales accounts using the modular model
Quantitative target: shorten median contract negotiation time by 30% for pilot accounts
tasks: Work with legal to draft modular contract clauses and sample SOW language (owner: Legal review)
Create pricing bands (Low/Med/High) with finance and forecast revenue impact (owner: Finance + PM)
Design SKUs and product metadata for billing/catalog systems (owner: Product Ops)
Build Security Questionnaire Response Pack: compile typical answers, mapping to internal controls (owner: Security)
Define operational runbook for Hotfix SLA and rolling upgrades (owner: Infra Ops)
Pilot with 2 willing customers and capture negotiation timeline/feedback (owner: Solutions Eng)
Update sales playbook and enablement materials (owner: GTM)
Instrument contract negotiation duration and close rate metrics for pilot cohort (owner: Analytics)
Create a simple Concur/Drive template bundle (contract + questionnaire + installation checklist) for pilots
notes: Trade-offs considered: exposing a Hotfix SLA increases operational risk and staffing needs; to mitigate we will limit Hotfix SLA to cores with a validated runbook and charge a significant premium. We considered tiered upgrade cadences (monthly/quarterly/annual) but selected quarterly by default with an option to opt into faster cadence for Priority customers. Finance prefers a multi-year discount for committed installs to improve ARR predictability.
updates: 2025-02-15: Kickoff meeting with Legal, Security, Finance, Solutions Eng. Agreed draft timeline and owners.
2025-02-20: Security completed initial mapping of common questionnaire items; identified 12 items that require product changes to answer affirmatively.
2025-02-27: Finance suggested three price bands tied to cluster size (small/medium/large); PM to model revenue impact.
2025-03-01: Infra Ops provided preliminary hotfix runbook and estimated 1.5 FTE operational cost for supporting 10 pilot customers. Decided to require Hotfix SLA opt-in and surcharge.
risks: Operational load from Hotfix SLA: increased paged incidents and on-call overhead
Legal negotiation: customers may request broader indemnity and longer maintenance commitments
Product gaps: answering security questionnaires may surface required product hardening work
Pricing complexity: too many SKUs could slow sales adoption
success_metrics: Contract negotiation time for pilot cohort reduced by >=30%
At least 2 pilot customers sign modular license + one support addon within 60 days
Support addon attach rate >25% for pilot cohort
No more than 2 unplanned hotfix incidents per pilot customer in first 3 months
